methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Emelody is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Thomas and Elizabeth Johnson that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of nine private robotics firms (including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though same-stage and adjacent-stage peers within the narrow robotics cohort are sparse.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable framework here. Using the $10M total capital raised as a proxy for entry valuation, a standard Growth-stage step-up multiplier of 1.2x yields $12M. A peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient filtered comparables—while ten same-sector robotics companies exist, none meet the thresholds of stage-alignment, valuation-tier proximity, or data density needed to generate a robust median.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This range reflects single-method confidence; the absence of tight-fit peer comps introduces material uncertainty around the precise multiple to apply at Growth stage. Key variables driving any upward or downward revision include revenue scale, capital efficiency metrics, and specific robotics subsector positioning relative to the identified peer set. Given data constraints, valuations outside the $10M–$14M band would require either new financial metrics or evidence of stage advancement beyond typical Growth-stage progression.
